test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 12 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
A ray of light is incident on a refracting surface AB of glass prism, Kept in air, and emerges out of the other refracting surface AC. Consider the following statements:

(a) The angle of refraction at surface AB is less than the angle of incidence.

(b) The angle of refraction at the surface AC is less than the angle of incidence.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (a)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phenomenon of change in the direction/path of light rays when it travel from one medium to another is called** refraction of light. **
 
• When light moves from air (n ≈ 1) to glass (n ≈ 1.5), it slows down and bends **towards the normal**.
 
• **The First Law of Refraction of Light** states that the incident ray, refracted ray, and normal to the interface at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.
 
• **The second Law of Refraction of Light **states that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence (i) and the sine of the angle of refraction (r) is constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The visible spectrum ranges from approximately** 400 nm (violet) to 700 nm (red)**. This is the portion of the spectrum visible to the human eye.
 
• **Light can be polarized by reflection**, scattering, or passing through polarizing filters.
 
• **Polarization** is used in sunglasses to reduce glare and in various optical devices.
 
• Light exhibits both **wave-like and particle-like properties, **leading to concepts like wave functions and photon behavior.
 
• The **frequency of visible light** ranges from about **400 THz (terahertz) for red light to about 789 THz for violet light.**
 
• The **energy of light photons increases with increasing frequency (or decreasing wavelength).**
